title: Time, Speed, Distance (Time)
instructions:
Problem: You are flying at a ground speed of 140 knots. How long will it take to travel 210 nautical miles?

1. Set the rate: Rotate the inner wheel to place the rate arrow (60) opposite 14 on the outer scale (for 140 knots).
2. Find distance: Locate 21 on the outer scale (for 210 NM).
3. Read time: Opposite 21 on the outer scale, read the time on the inner scale. The answer is 90 minutes (1 hour and 30 minutes).

title: Time, Speed, Distance (Speed)
instructions:
Problem: You have been flying for 45 minutes and have traveled 90 nautical miles. What is your ground speed?

1. Align time and distance: Rotate the inner wheel to place 45 (for 45 minutes) on the inner scale opposite 90 on the outer scale.
2. Read speed: Find the rate arrow (60) on the inner scale. It will point to your ground speed on the outer scale. The answer is 120 knots.

title: Time, Speed, Distance (Distance)
instructions:
Problem: You are flying at a ground speed of 110 knots. How far will you travel in 1 hour and 15 minutes (75 minutes)?

1. Set the rate: Rotate the inner wheel to place the rate arrow (60) opposite 11 on the outer scale (for 110 knots).
2. Find time: Locate 75 on the inner scale (for 75 minutes).
3. Read distance: Opposite 75 on the inner scale, read the distance on the outer scale. The answer is approximately 137.5 nautical miles.

title: Fuel Consumption (Fuel Used)
instructions:
Problem: Your aircraft consumes 12 gallons of fuel per hour. How much fuel will you use on a flight that takes 2 hours and 30 minutes (150 minutes)?

1. Set the rate: Rotate the inner wheel to place the rate arrow (60) opposite 12 on the outer scale (for 12 GPH).
2. Find time: Locate 15 on the inner scale (for 150 minutes).
3. Read fuel used: Opposite 15 on the inner scale, read the fuel consumed on the outer scale. The answer is 30 gallons.

title: Fuel Consumption (Endurance)
instructions:
Problem: Your aircraft has 48 gallons of usable fuel and consumes 15 gallons per hour. What is your maximum endurance?

1. Set the rate: Rotate the inner wheel to place the rate arrow (60) opposite 15 on the outer scale (for 15 GPH).
2. Find fuel: Locate 48 on the outer scale (for 48 gallons).
3. Read time: Opposite 48 on the outer scale, read the time on the inner scale. The answer is 192 minutes (3 hours and 12 minutes).

title: True Airspeed & Density Altitude
instructions:
Problem: Pressure altitude is 8,000 ft, OAT is -10°C, and Calibrated Airspeed (CAS) is 150 knots. Find TAS and Density Altitude.

1. Align Alt/Temp: In the Pressure Alt window, slide the wheel to align 8 (for 8,000 ft) with -10 on the temperature scale.
2. Find CAS: On the inner scale, locate 15 (for 150 knots CAS).
3. Read TAS: Opposite 15 on the inner scale, read the True Airspeed on the outer scale. The answer is approximately 165 knots.
4. Read Density Altitude: Look in the Density Altitude window. The arrow points to approximately 7,000 ft.

title: Nautical to Statute Miles
instructions:
Problem: Convert 75 nautical miles to statute miles.

1. Align distance: Rotate the inner wheel until 75 on the inner scale is aligned with the 'NAUT' mark on the outer scale.
2. Read conversion: The 'STAT' mark on the outer scale now points to the equivalent distance in statute miles on the inner scale (approx. 86.5).

title: Gallons to Liters
instructions:
Problem: Convert 30 US gallons to liters.

1. Align arrows: Rotate the inner wheel to align the 'US GAL' mark on the inner scale with 30 on the outer scale.
2. Read conversion: Find the 'LITERS' mark on the inner scale. The value on the outer scale opposite it is the volume in liters (approx. 113.5).
